calculatorUrlsAll: https://www.purdue.edu/impactearth/ (Impact: Earth! React app; physics runs client-side in static/js/main.a4859e04.js)
notes: 'expected' = full-precision outputs of the official Impact: Earth! calculator (Purdue build main.a4859e04.js): its calculation code was executed verbatim in Node.js, and the live web page, driven with the same inputs in a browser on 2026-10-04, displayed identical (rounded) values for all three cases. These follow Collins et al. (2005) + 2013 errata note (complex-crater depth 0.294 D^0.301 km) + Collins et al. (2017) airblast-energy rule. 'imperialServer' = values printed by the Imperial College server for the same inputs (unit-converted; display rounding 2-3 s.f.) plus values back-computed from its map radii (radians x 6371 km, inferred). The two official calculators DISAGREE on airblast overpressure/wind/arrival for crater-forming impacts (the Imperial server uses the unclamped negative airburst altitude, see 07-eiep.md sec. 7.4) and the Imperial server forces rho_t=2700 for crystalline rock. Calculator constants differ slightly from the paper (D_tc prefactor 1.16132 vs 1.161; 1 Mt = 4.186e15 J vs 4.18e15 J; g = 9.8 m/s2; R_E = 6370 km): a faithful implementation of the paper with paper constants differs by ~0.03% (crater diameters), ~0.1% (ejecta thickness, overpressure). Suggested tolerance: 0.5% relative for continuous quantities, 1e-3 absolute for magnitudes.

cases.crossCheck: Live Purdue page (2026-10-04) displayed: 2.72e23 J; Dtc 65.3 km; dtc 23.1 km; Dfr 113 km; dfr 1.23 km; melt 1.71e3 km3; thermal 3.64e7 J/m2; M 9.8; ejecta 8.24 min, 16.2 cm; 102000 Pa; 175 m/s - all equal to 'expected' after rounding. Imperial server agrees on energy, crater, melt, fireball radius, ejecta thickness and M (via its map radii) but prints 93467 Pa / 164.2 m/s for the airblast (see 07-eiep.md sec. 7.4).
cases.notes: thermalExposure includes horizon factor f=0.2801 (fireball partly below horizon at 1000 km). magnitude uses impact (surface) energy 2.7192e23 J, not entry energy. Meff from Eq. 41c with Delta in radians.
